ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r2.claim: والذي جعل لكم is God's speech, reminding people of earlier blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r2.anchor: والذي جعل لكم: من كلام الله، خطابا لهم بتذكير نعمه السابقة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r5.claim: لعلكم تهتدون can mean finding one's destinations in travel or gaining guidance through reflection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r5.anchor: لعلكم تهتدون: أي إلى مقاصدكم في السفر، أو تهتدون بالنظر والاعتبار.

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.claim: The surah challenges the worldview of the Makkan idolaters, answering their objections and addressing forms of disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.anchor: The first half of the sūrah responds to different objections that the Makkan idolaters are reported to have posed to the message of the Quran

NAHHAS:v4p98/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p98/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p98/r7.claim: Alladhī is nominative either as an adjective of al-ʿazīz or with an omitted subject.
NAHHAS:v4p98/r7.anchor: الذي في موضع رفع على النعت للعزيز أو على إضمار مبتدأ لأنه أول آية

ASAD-NOTES:43:9#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:9#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:9#n8/r1.claim: Asad cross-references the earth made as a cradle to 20:53.

QIRAAT-ER:43:10:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:43:10:5#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:43:10:5#1/r1.claim: The variant mihādan replaces mahdan, emphasizing bedding or prepared spreading.
QIRAAT-ER:43:10:5#1/r1.anchor: Lvw, mutawatir: Canonical variant replaces مَهْدًا (mahdan) with مِهَادًا (mihādan)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#3/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the paths made through the earth as roads.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p194#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وجعل لكم فيها سبلا ﴾ قال طرقا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r1.claim: The earth is made a leveled, prepared place for people to settle; its spherical shape does not conflict with this because of its immense size.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r1.anchor: مكانا ممهدا أي موطأ ومآله بسطها لكم تستقرون فيها ولا ينافي ذلك كرتها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r2.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r2.claim: Asim reads the word without an alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r2.anchor: وعن عاصم أنه قرأ ( مهدا ) بدون ألف

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r3.claim: The paths are routes to destinations and can also lead by reflection to monotheism, the primary goal.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#4/r3.anchor: أي لكي تهتدوا بسلوكها إلى مقاصدكم أو بالتفكر فيها إلى التوحيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r1.claim: After the preceding account, God begins demonstrating His existence through His works: He made the earth a resting place and roads so travelers can reach their destinations.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r1.anchor: ثم ابتدأ دالا على نفسه بصنعه فقال: {الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون} إلى مقاصدكم في أسفاركم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r2.claim: The roads through the earth enable people to find their destinations on journeys.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r2.anchor: وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون} إلى مقاصدكم في أسفاركم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r6.claim: God made the earth a resting place where people settle.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r6.anchor: جعل لكم الأرض مهدا } فتستقرون فيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r7.claim: Readers outside Kufa read مهادا with a long alif.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r1.claim: The paths through the earth are routes for people to travel.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r2.claim: People may reach their destinations by them, or recognize the Creator's wisdom through reflection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r2.anchor: لكي تهتدوا إلى مقاصدكم، أو إلى حكمة الصانع

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r4.claim: The shift to direct address makes the rebuke sharper and reminds the questioners of the kindness that should lead them to submit.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r4.anchor: أتبعهما من كلامه دلالة على ذلك قوله التفاتا إلى الخطاب لأنه أمكن في التقريع والتوبيخ والتشنيع

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r5.claim: The earth is like a bed: settled, firm, and level; God could instead have made it quake or made it unstable like something carried on flowing water.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r6.claim: As God made the earth a settled place for bodies, he made bodies a settled place for spirits, fitting them for presence and travel and showing his rule over the cosmos.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r6.anchor: ولما جعل الأرض قرارا لأشباحكم جعل الأشباح قرارا لأرواحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r7.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r7.claim: Al-Qushayri analogizes the earth’s eventual ruin after the souls’ earthly term with the ruin of bodies when their spirits depart.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r7.anchor: قال القشيري : فإذا انتهى مدة كون النفوس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r8.claim: Repeating جعل emphasizes God’s ability to establish means that make difficult tasks easy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r8.anchor: وأعاد الفعل تنبيها على تمكنه تعالى من إقامة الأسباب لتيسير الأمور الصعاب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r1.claim: The paths are routes through mountains and valleys; God could instead have made the land impassable, as some mountains are.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r1.anchor: ولو شاء لجعلها بحيث لا يسلك في مكان منها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r2.claim: The paths let people find destinations in worldly affairs, travel to distant lands and broad regions, and reach useful aims; repeated use makes the routes themselves guide travelers.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r2.anchor: فتتوصلون بها إلى الأقطار الشاسعة والأقاليم الواسعة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r3.claim: Beyond practical navigation, an intelligent observer can be guided by reflecting on the wisdom of the One who subjected and arranged the world.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r3.anchor: وحكمتها باطنا إذا تأمل الفطن حكمة مسخرها وواضعها وميسرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r1.claim: The passage moves from proof that God alone created heaven and earth to proof He alone provides life's necessities; this resumption interrupts the transition to 43:15.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r1.anchor: هو تخلص من الاستدلال على تفرده بالإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r2.claim: The sentence resumes with an omitted subject, هو الذي جعل لكم; the relative noun is the predicate of that understood subject.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r3.claim: Following al-Sakkaki's terminology, subject omission follows established usage; the relative pronoun is famous through its clause and functions like a proper name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r3.anchor: وهو من حذف المسند إليه الوارد على متابعة الاستعمال في تسمية السكاكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r4.claim: Both relative clauses show God's exclusive power and beneficence; لكم is inserted twice to signal human benefit, unlike 78:6–7, which argues from great creation to resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r4.anchor: وذكرت صلتان فيهما دلالة على الانفراد بالقدرة العظيمة وعلى النعمة عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r5.claim: The relative noun is not repeated before making paths because both clauses concern the earth and form one imagined act.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r5.anchor: لأن الصلتين تجتمعان في الجامع الخيالي إذ كلتاهما من أحوال الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.claim: The eleven second-person pronouns across these four verses follow the expected address and are not iltifat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.anchor: وضمائر الخطاب الأحد عشر الواقعة في الآيات الأربع من قوله : { الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهادا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r7.claim: مهاد means something prepared, leveled, and made easy to dwell on; the earth's flattened surface benefits human inhabitants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r7.anchor: والمهاد : اسم لشيء يمهد ، أي يوطأ ويسهل لما يحل فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r8.claim: Calling the earth a level resting place does not conflict with its spherical body; its spherical shape itself is not the feature benefiting people here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r8.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي أن جسم الأرض كروي كما هو ظاهر لأن كرويتها ليست منفعة للناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r9.speaker: عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r9.claim: Asim reads مهدا without an alif after hāʾ, with the same intended sense as مهاد.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r9.anchor: وقرأ عاصم مهدا } بدون ألف بعد الهاء وهو مراد به المهاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.claim: These descriptions of God's acts are blessings to humanity and proof against every disbelieving polytheist.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.anchor: على كل كافر مشرك بالله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r2.claim: The phrase begins a fresh divine report, not part of the questioners' speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r2.anchor: بل هو ابتداء إخبار من الله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r3.claim: Most readers have مهادا; Ibn Masud, Talha, and al-A'mash read مهدا, and the two forms have the same sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن مسعود وطلحة والأعمش: «مهدا» ، والمعنى واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r4.claim: The earth is a prepared, spread-out place in which people can settle and move about.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى واحد، أي يتمهد ويتصرف فيها.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r5.anchor: والسبل: الطرق. و: تهتدون معناه في المقاصد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r6.claim: One possible sense is finding one's way from one town or region to another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r6.anchor: تهتدون معناه في المقاصد من بلد إلى بلد ومن قطر إلى قطر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, guidance may mean being guided by reflection and consideration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد: تهتدون بالنظر والاعتبار.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r1.claim: The following passage is explained at Ta-Ha 53 through this phrase.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r1.anchor: ثم التي تليها مفسرة في طه 53 إلى قوله ﴿ لعلكم تهتدون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r2.claim: The paths are provided so that people may find their destinations while travelling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#4/r2.anchor: أي لكي تهتدوا في أسفاركم إلى مقاصدكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r2.claim: The earth is a stable bed where people walk, stand, sleep and go about; though created upon flowing water, God fixed it with mountains so it does not sway.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r2.anchor: أي: فراشا قرارا ثابتة، يسيرون عليها ويقومون وينامون وينصرفون، مع أنها مخلوقة على تيار الماء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r3.claim: God made routes through mountains and valleys so people can find their way from one town, region and territory to another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r3.anchor: أي: طرقا بين الجبال والأودية {لعلكم تهتدون} أي: في سيركم من بلد إلى بلد، وقطر إلى قطر،

BURSEVI:v8p271/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271/r1.claim: The relative clause is a fresh statement from God; jaʿala means to make something one way rather than another.
BURSEVI:v8p271/r1.anchor: {الذى جعل لكم الارض مهدا} استئناف من جهته تعالى. والجعل بمعنى تصيير الشيء على حاله دون حالة

BURSEVI:v8p271/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271/r2.claim: Mahd and mihad mean a prepared, smoothed place; God spread the earth as a place where people settle, as in 2:22.
BURSEVI:v8p271/r2.anchor: والمهد والمهاد المكان الممهد الموطأ لقوله تعالى : {جعل لكم الارض فراشا} (البقرة : 22) ؛ أي : بسطها لكم تستقرون فيها

BURSEVI:v8p271/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271/r3.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v8p271/r3.claim: Bahr al-ʿUlum says the earth is a dwelling where people sit, sleep, and turn over as on a bed.
BURSEVI:v8p271/r3.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : جعل الأرض مسكنا لكم تقعدون عليها وتنامون وتنقلبون كما ينقلب أحدكم على فراشه ومهاده.

BURSEVI:v8p271/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271/r4.claim: The paths are familiar routes people travel for worldly and religious purposes.
BURSEVI:v8p271/r4.anchor: {وجعل لكم فيها سبلا} تسلكونها في أسفاركم لأمور الدين والدنيا جمع سبيل

BURSEVI:v8p271/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p271/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines a path as a route that is easy to traverse.
BURSEVI:v8p271/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب : السبيل الطريق الذي فيه سهولة.

BURSEVI:v8p271/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271/r6.claim: The routes lead to people's destinations, or reflection on the earth guides them to the primary goal of divine unity.
BURSEVI:v8p271/r6.anchor: {لعلكم تهتدون} ؛ أي : لكي تهتدوا لسلوكها إلى مقاصدكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.claim: God made the earth a resting spread for people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r1.anchor: { الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا } أي فراشا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r2.claim: The paths may also mean means of livelihood.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā says this guidance is finding one’s way on journeys.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r3.anchor: تهتدون في أسفاركم , قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says it is recognizing God’s favor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r4.anchor: تعرفون نعمة الله عليكم , قاله سعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p216#2/r5.claim: Al-Māwardī also allows guidance to one’s livelihoods.

MUQATIL:43:8-10/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r4.claim: God made the earth a bed or floor for people.
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r4.anchor: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا } ، يعني فرشا

MUQATIL:43:8-10/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r5.claim: The paths are routes people travel.
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r5.anchor: وجعل لكم فيها سبلا } ، يعني طرقا تسلكونها

MUQATIL:43:8-10/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r6.claim: The paths let people recognize their routes.
MUQATIL:43:8-10/r6.anchor: لعلكم تهتدون } [آية: 10]، يقول: لكي تعرفوا طرقها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r1.speaker: كوفي وغيره
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r1.claim: The Kufans read mahdan; the other readers have mihādan, meaning a place of rest.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r1.anchor: كوفى وغيره مهادا اى موضع قرار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r2.claim: God made routes in the earth so that people can find their way on journeys.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#7/r2.anchor: ﴿ لعلكم تهتدون ﴾ لكى تهتدوا في اسفاركم

QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r1.claim: God describes His complete power; this begins His own declaration, since a report quoting the unbelievers would have said that He made the earth a resting place for us.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r1.anchor: وهذا ابتداء إخبار منه عن نفسه، ولو كان هذا إخبارا عن قول الكفار لقال الذي جعل لنا الأرض { مهدا } فراشا وبساطا.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم. وقرأ الكوفيون «مهدا» { وجعل لكم فيها سبلا } أي معايش

QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r3.claim: One interpretation takes the paths as means of livelihood; another takes them as roads for traveling wherever one wishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r3.anchor: أي معايش. وقيل طرقا، لتسلكوا منها إلى حيث أردتم

QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r4.claim: The paths allow people to infer God's power from His created works.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r5.claim: Ibn Isa says the phrase means that you may find your way during journeys.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r5.anchor: وقيل: «لعلكم تهتدون» في أسفاركم قاله ابن عيسى

QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the phrase means that you may recognize God's blessing upon you.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r6.anchor: وقيل: لعلكم تعرفون نعمة الله عليكم قاله سعيد بن جبير

QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:10/r7.claim: Another explanation is that people may find their means of livelihood.

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r3.claim: The speech then shifts to God describing His own works: idolaters would have said “for us,” not “for you,” and the first-person “We revived” likewise belongs to God's speech.

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r4.claim: He illustrates the shift with one speaker naming a mosque's builder and a listener adding further praise: both descriptions concern the same person though they come from different speakers.
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r4.anchor: ونظيره من كلام الناس يأن يسمع الرجل رجلا يقول الذي بنى هذا المسجد فلان العالم

RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r8.claim: Earth is a resting place because it is stable and has properties that permit cultivation, construction, and concealment of the flaws of living and dead people; like a child's cradle, it offers many comforts.
RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r8.anchor: كون الأرض مهدا إنما حصل لأجل كونها واقفة ساكنة ولأجل كونها موصوفة بصفات مخصوصة باعتبارها يمكن الانتفاع بها في الزراعة وبناء الأبنية

RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r1.claim: God provides roads so people can travel from town to town and region to region; without the routes and their identifying markers, this benefit would not be possible.
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r1.anchor: انتفاع الناس إنما يكمل إذا قدر كل أحد أن يذهب من بلد إلى بلد ومن إقليم إلى إقليم

RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r2.claim: “So that you may be guided” means both that people can find their way along the routes and that they may be guided to religious truth.
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r2.anchor: قال تعالى : { لعلكم تهتدون } يعني المقصود من وضع السبل أن يحصل لكم المكنة من الاهتداء ، والثاني المعنى لتهتدوا إلى الحق في الدين

STUDYQURAN:43:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r1.claim: The earth as a cradle means it is smooth and easy to travel upon.
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r1.anchor: That God made the earth a cradle means He made the earth smooth, easy to travel upon

STUDYQURAN:43:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r2.claim: The earth is also made tractable for agriculture and a home for human life.
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r2.anchor: tractable for agriculture (R), and a home for human life.

STUDYQURAN:43:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r3.claim: The paths are navigable routes God made upon the earth.
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r3.anchor: refers to navigable routes He has made upon it (IK, JJ).

STUDYQURAN:43:10/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r4.claim: In context, guidance means God facilitates earthly travel and provides signs and revelation leading to truth and Paradise in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:43:10/r4.anchor: God both facilitates travel upon the earth in this life and provides signs and revelation to guide human beings to truth and to Paradise

TAB-FULL:v20p554/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r2.claim: Allah made the earth a spread-out bed for people to walk and tread upon.
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r2.anchor: الذي مهد لكم الأرض، فجعلها لكم وطاء توطئونها بأقدامكم، وتمشون عليها بأرجلكم

TAB-FULL:v20p554/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r3.claim: Allah made easy routes from town to town for people’s livelihoods and trade.
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r3.anchor: وسهل لكم فيها طرقا تتطرقونها من بلدة إلى بلدة، لمعايشكم ومتاجركم

TAB-FULL:v20p554/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r4.claim: Qatāda glosses the paths as routes.
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {وجعل لكم فيها سبلا} [الزخرف: 10] «أي طرقا»

TAB-FULL:v20p554/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r5.claim: Al-Suddī calls the earth a carpet and the paths roads.
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r5.anchor: عن السدي، {الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا} [طه: 53] قال: «بساطا» {وجعل لكم فيها سبلا} [الزخرف: 10] قال: «الطرق»

TAB-FULL:v20p554/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r6.claim: The roads let people reach their intended lands, villages, and cities; without them they could not leave their courtyards and homes, so the roads are a blessing.
TAB-FULL:v20p554/r6.anchor: لكي تهتدوا بتلك السبل إلى حيث أردتم من البلدان والقرى والأمصار، لولا ذلك لم تطيقوا براح أفنيتكم ودوركم

TABATABAI:43:6-10/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r9.claim: God made the earth a place where people are nurtured, as children are raised in a cradle.
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r9.anchor: أي جعل لكم الأرض بحيث تربون فيها كما يربى الأطفال في المهد

TABATABAI:43:6-10/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r10.claim: God placed roads in the earth for people to travel and find their destinations.
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r10.anchor: وجعل لكم في الأرض سبلا وطرقا تسلكونها

TABATABAI:43:6-10/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r11.claim: An alternative takes ‘so that you may be guided’ to mean guidance to knowledge of God and worshipping Him alone; the author prefers guidance along roads.
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r11.anchor: وقيل معنى { لعلكم تهتدون } رجاء أن تهتدوا إلى معرفة الله

TABATABAI:43:6-10/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r12.claim: The shift to address the people emphasizes that governance belongs with creation; admitting God alone creates while others govern is incoherent, and direct address rebukes them.
TABATABAI:43:6-10/r12.anchor: وفي الكلام التفات إلى خطاب القوم بعد صرف الخطاب عنهم

TABRISI:43:6-10/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:6-10/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:6-10/r6.claim: An alternative reading is mihadan; al-Tabrisi says its explanation was already given in Ta Ha.
TABRISI:43:6-10/r6.anchor: وقرئ مهادا وقد مضى ذكره في طه

TABRISI:43:6-10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:6-10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:6-10/r7.claim: God made paths through the land so people can travel and find their destinations.
TABRISI:43:6-10/r7.anchor: لكي تهتدوا إلى مقاصدكم في أسفاركم

TABRISI:43:6-10/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:6-10/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:43:6-10/r8.claim: A further explanation is that reflecting on the land guides people to religious truth.
TABRISI:43:6-10/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه لتهتدوا إلى الحق في الدين بالاعتبار الذي حصل لكم بالنظر فيها

THALABI:v8p328/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p328/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p328/r10.claim: God made the earth a cradle and set paths through it so people could find their way.
THALABI:v8p328/r10.anchor: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.claim: After finishing the report of their answer, God begins describing Himself in the following verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4.anchor: وقد تم الإخبار عنهم (¬5) ثم ابتدأ جل وعز دالا على نفسه فقال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the speech shifts from the unbelievers' reported answer to God's own description; otherwise they would say “for us,” not “for you.” The two attributes still describe the same God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1.anchor: قال صاحب # النظم: أخبر الله عما يقول الكفار إذا سئلوا عمن خلق السموات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r1.claim: The land-making clause adds a true attribute to the attribute quoted from the unbelievers; its explanation was given at Ṭā Hā 20:53.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r1.anchor: صفة من صفاته أضافها -عز وجل- إلى الصفة التي حكاها عن الكفار؛ لأنها حق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r2.speaker: الحسن ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r2.claim: Hasan and Muqatil take the guidance as finding one's destination while travelling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r2.anchor: أحدهما: تهتدون في أسفاركم إلى مقاصدكم، وهذا قول الحسن ومقاتل،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas understands the guidance as reaching the truth by reflecting on the land God provided.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r1.claim: From this verse, the passage exposes contradictions and unsupported beliefs in the polytheists' thinking and indirectly calls them to monotheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r1.anchor: Bu âyetten itibaren müşriklerin düşüncelerindeki çelişkilere, inançlarındaki temelsizliğe dikkat çekilmekte ve onlar dolaylı olarak tevhide davet edilmektedirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r2.claim: Making the earth a bed means making it suitable for walking, working, resting, and living.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r2.anchor: Yerin döşek kılınmasından maksat üzerinde yürümeye, çalışmaya ve istirahat etmeye; yani yaşamaya uygun bir şekilde olmasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r3.claim: One reading of paths is terrain such as valleys, plains, and passes that permits travel from one place to another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r3.anchor: Dünyanın bir yerinden diğer yerine ulaşmayı mümkün kılacak vadilerin, düzlüklerin, geçitlerin yani üzerinde yürümeye ve yol açmaya müsait arazinin yaratılması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r4.claim: Taking subul as means or remedies, the paths are the resources created to meet people's varied needs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:10/r4.anchor: Kelimenin ikinci (vesîle, çare) mânasına göre yaratılan yollardan maksat, insanların çeşitli ihtiyaçlarını giderecek imkânların yaratılmasıdır

BURHAN:v1p130/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r10.claim: Ṭā Hā uses وسلك لكم فيها سبلا, while al-Zukhruf uses وجعل لكم فيها سبلا.
BURHAN:v1p130/r10.anchor: فى طه ﴿ وسلك لكم فيها سبلا ﴾ وفى الزخرف ﴿ وجعل لكم فيها سبلا ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.claim: These readers use مهدا with alif throughout the Qurʾān; ʿĀṣim, Hamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit it in Ṭā Hā and al-Zukhruf.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r6.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر ﴿ مهدا ﴾ بالألف فى كل القرآن

NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.claim: In الأرض مهادا in Taha and al-Zukhruf, the Kufans use fatḥa on mīm and a quiescent hāʾ without alif; the others use kasra on mīm, fatḥa on hāʾ, and a following alif. Ibn Mihran's report from Rawh is an error.
NASHR:v2p319#2/r6.anchor: فقرأ الكوفيون بفتح الميم، وإسكان الهاء من غير ألف
